title.zh: 卷253 列傳四十 莫洛 陈福 王之鼎 李兴元 陈启泰 陈丹赤 葉映榴
title.en: Volume 253 Biographies 40: Mo Luo, Chen Fu, Wang Zhiding, Li Xingyuan, Chen Qitai, Chen Danchi, Ye Yingliu
title.raw: 卷253 列傳四十 莫洛 陈福 王之鼎 李兴元 陈启泰 陈丹赤 葉映榴

sentences.zh: =莫洛=莫洛，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲正紅旗人，世居呼納赫魯。

translations.literal: Mo Luo, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner, whose family had long resided at Hunahuru.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Luo, of the Irgen Gioro clan, came from the Plain Red Banner Manchus; his family had long lived at Hunahuru.

sentences.zh: 祖溫察，太祖時來歸。

translations.literal: His ancestor Wenca came over and submitted in the time of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Wenca submitted during the reign of Taizu (Nurhaci).

sentences.zh: 莫洛初授刑部理事官，累遷工部郎中。

translations.literal: Mo Luo was first appointed a clerk in the Board of Punishments and was promoted repeatedly until he became a director in the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Luo began as a clerk in the Board of Punishments and rose through successive posts to director in the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi, he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 (1667), he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 七年，出為山西陝西總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he went out to serve as Governor-General of Shanxi and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Governor-General of Shanxi and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 陝西飢，平涼、臨洮、鞏昌、西安、延安、鳳翔、漢中、興安諸府州多逋賦，有司令現戶均輸，民苦之，奏請蠲免。

translations.literal: Shaanxi suffered famine; in Pingliang, Lintao, Gongchang, Xi'an, Yan'an, Fengxiang, Hanzhong, Xing'an, and other prefectures and departments there was much arrears in tax, and some officials ordered that present households should pay equally, which afflicted the people; he memorialized requesting exemption.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Shaanxi, many prefectures and departments—including Pingliang, Lintao, Gongchang, Xi'an, Yan'an, Fengxiang, Hanzhong, and Xing'an—had large tax arrears. Some officials ordered current households to share the burden equally, to the people's distress; Mo Luo memorialized asking that these levies be remitted.

sentences.zh: 迭疏清釐加派、火耗諸弊。

translations.literal: He submitted memorial after memorial to clear up abuses such as surcharges and meltage fees.
translations.idiomatic: He sent repeated memorials to root out abuses such as extra assessments and meltage surcharges.

sentences.zh: 八年，輔政大臣鼇拜獲譴，法司以莫洛附鼇拜，請逮問，詔以能任事，貸勿治，仍留任。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the regent Oboi was punished; the judicial authorities, on the ground that Mo Luo had attached himself to Oboi, requested that he be arrested and questioned; an edict said that because he was capable in office, he was pardoned and not prosecuted, and he remained in his post.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8 (1669), when the regent Oboi fell, the judiciary charged Mo Luo with having sided with Oboi and asked that he be arrested and tried. The throne ruled that, as he was capable in office, he should be pardoned and left in his post.

sentences.zh: 九年，計典，仍以前罪奪職。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, at the triennial evaluation, he was still deprived of office on account of the former offense.
translations.idiomatic: At the triennial evaluation in Kangxi 9 (1670), he was again stripped of office for the earlier offense.

sentences.zh: 陝西民籥留，甘肅巡撫劉鬥同，提督張勇、柏永馥等疏言莫洛清正，在官有善政，乞留以慰民望。

translations.literal: The people of Shaanxi detained him with bamboos in farewell; Gansu Governor Liu Dou and Regional Commanders Zhang Yong, Bai Yongfu, and others memorialized that Mo Luo was upright and clear, that in office he had good policies, and begged that he be kept to comfort the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shaanxi bade him stay with the farewell rite of detaining his carriage; Gansu Governor Liu Dou, together with Regional Commanders Zhang Yong and Bai Yongfu, memorialized that Mo Luo was upright and had governed well, asking that he be retained to satisfy popular expectation.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「簡用督撫，原以綏輯地方，愛養百姓。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed, saying: 'In selecting governors-general and governors, the original purpose is to pacify and put in order the regions and to cherish and nurture the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: 'Governors-general and governors are chosen in the first place to bring peace to the regions and to care for the people.

sentences.zh: 莫洛既能得民，其免處分，供職如故。

translations.literal: Since Mo Luo has been able to win the people, let him be exempted from punishment and continue in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Since Mo Luo has won the people's trust, let the penalty be waived and let him serve on as before.

sentences.zh: 」俄擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: ' Shortly afterward he was promoted to Minister of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: ' Soon after he was promoted to Minister of the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十三年，吳三桂等奏請撤籓，上敕廷臣議，皆主勿徙，惟莫洛與米思翰、明珠議撤。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Wu Sangui and others memorialized requesting the abolition of the feudatories; the Emperor ordered the court ministers to deliberate; all advocated that they not be moved, and only Mo Luo, together with Misihan and Mingzhu, argued for abolition.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 (1674), when Wu Sangui and others asked that the princely fiefs be abolished, the Emperor ordered the court to debate the matter. Nearly all favored leaving the fiefs in place; only Mo Luo, Misihan, and Mingzhu argued for abolition.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，四川提督鄭蛟麟等叛應之。

translations.literal: Sangui rebelled, and Sichuan Provincial Military Commissioner Zheng Jiaolin and others rebelled in response.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui rose in rebellion, and Sichuan Provincial Military Commissioner Zheng Jiaolin and others joined him.

sentences.zh: 二月，命莫洛經略陝西，拜武英殿大學士，仍管兵部，賜以敕印，既至，策遣諸軍徵四川。

translations.literal: In the second month, Mo Luo was ordered to take charge of military affairs in Shaanxi, was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, and still supervised the Board of War; he was granted an imperial commission and seal; when he arrived, he planned and dispatched the armies to campaign against Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was made commissioner for Shaanxi, appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory while continuing to head the Board of War, and given an imperial commission and seal. On reaching his post he drew up plans and sent the armies into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時蛟麟兵據廣元百丈關，莫洛遣都統馬一寶、將軍席卜臣赴漢中，副都統科爾寬赴廣元，擊賊。

translations.literal: At that time Jiaolin's troops held the Baizhang Pass at Guangyuan; Mo Luo sent Commandant-in-Chief Ma Yibao and General Xibuchen to Hanzhong, and Vice Commandant-in-Chief Ke'erkuang to Guangyuan, to attack the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaolin's forces then held Baizhang Pass at Guangyuan. Mo Luo sent Commandant-in-Chief Ma Yibao and General Xibuchen to Hanzhong and Vice Commandant-in-Chief Ke'erkuang to Guangyuan to strike the rebels.

sentences.zh: 十月，蛟麟將何德成犯寧羌，為官軍所敗，還奔四川，莫洛因遣提督王輔臣駐其地。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Jiaolin's general He Decheng invaded Ningqiang, was defeated by the government troops, and fled back to Sichuan; Mo Luo therefore sent Regional Commander Wang Fuchen to garrison that place.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Jiaolin's general He Decheng attacked Ningqiang, was beaten by government forces, and fled back into Sichuan. Mo Luo then sent Regional Commander Wang Fuchen to hold the area.

sentences.zh: 踰月，蛟麟將彭時亨复據七盤、百丈諸關，劫略陽糧艘，截陸運棧道。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Jiaolin's general Peng Shiheng again seized the passes at Qipan, Baizhang, and elsewhere, plundered grain boats at Lueyang, and cut the overland transport plank road.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month Jiaolin's general Peng Shiheng had retaken Qipan, Baizhang, and other passes, raided grain convoys at Lueyang, and blocked the overland supply route.

sentences.zh: 廣元軍缺餉兩月矣，總兵王懷忠所部潰散，而輔臣亦陰懷異志。

translations.literal: The army at Guangyuan had lacked pay for two months; the troops under Brigadier Wang Huaizhong had scattered in rout, and Fuchen also secretly harbored disloyal intentions.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangyuan army had gone two months without pay; Brigadier Wang Huaizhong's command had broken and fled; and Fuchen was already nursing secret disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 輔臣故與莫洛有郄，奉檄使隨徵，益怏怏，藉口戎備寡，莫洛益以騎兵二千，少之；

translations.literal: Fuchen had long had a grudge against Mo Luo; ordered by commission to campaign with him, he grew still more resentful, alleging on the pretext that military preparations were scant; Mo Luo added two thousand cavalry for him, which he regarded as too few;
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen had old grievances against Mo Luo. Ordered to campaign under him, he grew still more sullen and complained that his forces were too weak. Mo Luo gave him two thousand more cavalry, which he still deemed insufficient;

sentences.zh: 又以馬疲瘠不任用搖軍心，軍無鬥志。

translations.literal: he also, on the ground that the horses were lean and worn and unusable, shook the army's morale, and the troops had no fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: he also refused to use the lean, worn horses provided, unsettling the troops until the army lost all will to fight.

sentences.zh: 十二月，莫洛至寧羌，兩營相去二里許。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Mo Luo reached Ningqiang; the two camps were about two li apart.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Mo Luo reached Ningqiang, his camp and Fuchen's standing about two li apart.

sentences.zh: 先是，上命莫洛統綠營步旅下四川，嗣慮巴蜀道險，令貝勒洞鄂率滿洲騎兵兼程繼進。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor had ordered Mo Luo to lead Green Standard infantry south into Sichuan; afterward, fearing the dangerous roads of Ba and Shu, he ordered Prince Dong'e to lead Manchu cavalry to follow by forced marches.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor had ordered Mo Luo to lead Green Standard foot troops into Sichuan. Fearing the difficult Ba-Shu routes, he then ordered Prince Dong'e to follow at forced march with Manchu cavalry.

sentences.zh: 軍未至，是月庚寅朔，癸巳，輔臣煽所部噪餉，襲劫莫洛。

translations.literal: The army had not yet arrived; on the first day gengyin of that month, on guisi, Fuchen incited his troops to clamor for pay and made a surprise attack on Mo Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Before those reinforcements arrived, on the third day of the month Fuchen stirred his men to riot over pay and launched a surprise attack on Mo Luo.

sentences.zh: 莫洛督兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: Mo Luo personally directed the troops and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Luo led his troops and beat them off.

sentences.zh: 甫定，輔臣复率悍黨至，砲矢雨坌，莫洛被創，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Hardly had order been restored when Fuchen again led fierce partisans up; cannon shot and arrows fell like rain; Mo Luo was wounded and died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the first assault been repelled when Fuchen returned with hardened followers; shot and arrows fell like rain; Mo Luo was wounded and died in the field.

sentences.zh: 卹典久未行，二十二年，命予祭葬，諡忠愍，授世職拜他喇布勒哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Funeral honors were long delayed; in the twenty-second year, he was ordered to receive sacrificial burial, was given the posthumous title Zhongmin (Loyal and Sorrowful), and was granted the hereditary rank of Baturu Bannerman together with Tosaha Bannerman.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral honors were long delayed. In Kangxi 22 (1683) he was granted sacrificial burial, given the posthumous title Zhongmin (Loyal and Sorrowful), and awarded the combined hereditary ranks of Baturu Bannerman and Tosaha Bannerman.

sentences.zh: 子常安，襲。

translations.literal: His son Chang'an inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang'an inherited the title.

sentences.zh: =陳福=陳福，字箕演，陝西榆林人。

translations.literal: Chen Fu, style name Jiyan, was a native of Yulin in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fu, style name Jiyan, came from Yulin in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 國初師定陝西，福以武舉應募，從寧夏總兵劉芳名剿寇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty, when the army pacified Shaanxi, Fu enlisted as a military licentiate and followed Ningxia Brigadier Liu Fangming in suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's early campaigns to pacify Shaanxi, Fu enlisted as a military licentiate and served under Ningxia Brigadier Liu Fangming against bandits.

sentences.zh: 敘功，授守備。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was appointed garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was appointed garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 又從都統李國翰下四川，遷遵義游擊。

translations.literal: He again followed Commandant-in-Chief Li Guohan into Sichuan and was transferred to be mobile battalion commander at Zunyi.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Commandant-in-Chief Li Guohan into Sichuan and was made mobile battalion commander at Zunyi.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，從總督李國英討李自成遺黨郝搖旗、李來亨等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi, he followed Governor Li Guoying in campaigning against the remnants of Li Zicheng's party, Hao Yaoqi, Li Laiheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi he campaigned under Governor Li Guoying against Li Zicheng's remaining followers Hao Yaoqi, Li Laiheng, and the like.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加右都督銜，擢成都副將，遷重慶總兵。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; he was given the brevet rank of Right Censor-in-Chief, was promoted to deputy commander at Chengdu, and was transferred to brigadier at Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he received the brevet rank of Right Censor-in-Chief, was promoted to deputy commander at Chengdu, and then to brigadier at Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 十二年，入覲，授寧夏總兵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he came to court for audience and was appointed brigadier at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 (1673) he attended court and was appointed brigadier at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，鄭蛟麟以四川叛應之，遣使誘福。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui rebelled; Zheng Jiaolin rebelled in Sichuan in response and sent envoys to entice Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Zheng Jiaolin rose in Sichuan in support and sent envoys to win Fu over.

sentences.zh: 福家留重慶，弟奇官守備，妻子亦在賊中，賊以是劫福。

translations.literal: Fu's family remained at Chongqing; his younger brother Qi held the post of garrison commander, and his wife and children were also in rebel hands; the rebels used this to coerce Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's family had stayed behind at Chongqing; his brother Qi was a garrison commander, and his wife and children were in rebel hands. The rebels used them to pressure Fu.

sentences.zh: 福執其使，具疏入告，遣其弟諸生壽齎詣京師。

translations.literal: Fu seized their envoy, drew up a full memorial reporting the matter, and sent his younger brother, the student Shou, to carry it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fu seized the envoy, wrote a full report, and sent his younger brother Shou, a licentiate, to deliver it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上嘉福忠，授拜他喇布勒哈番，並官壽主事。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised Fu's loyalty, granted him the rank of Baturu Bannerman, and also appointed Shou a secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor commended Fu's loyalty, granted him the rank of Baturu Bannerman, and appointed Shou a secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 輔臣據平涼，福上戰守方略。

translations.literal: Fuchen held Pingliang; Fu submitted plans for offense and defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuchen held Pingliang, Fu submitted plans for attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢陝西提督，進三等阿思哈尼哈番，又官奇參將。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was promoted to Provincial Military Commissioner of Shaanxi, advanced to third-rank Ashan-i Bannerman, and his brother Qi was also made deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 (1675) he was made Provincial Military Commissioner of Shaanxi and raised to third-rank Ashan-i Bannerman; his brother Qi was appointed deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 進規花馬池，惠安、安定、定邊諸城堡，以次皆下。

translations.literal: He advanced to invest Huamachi and the fortresses at Hui'an, Anding, Dingbian, and elsewhere; they fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Huamachi and the fortresses at Hui'an, Anding, Dingbian, and elsewhere, taking them in succession.

sentences.zh: 上擢壽鴻臚寺少卿。

translations.literal: The Emperor promoted Shou to Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor promoted Shou to Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 福率副將泰必圖乘勝薄固原，圍之匝月。

translations.literal: Fu led Deputy Commander Taibitu to press on the victory and close in on Guyuan, besieging it for a full month.
translations.idiomatic: Fu led Deputy Commander Taibitu in a victorious push against Guyuan and besieged the city for a full month.

sentences.zh: 輔臣遣其將來援，城賊亦突出，泰必圖戰死。

translations.literal: Fuchen sent his generals to relieve the city; the rebels in the city also sallied forth; Taibitu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen sent generals to relieve the city, and the defenders sallied out as well; Taibitu was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 福引兵還靈州，斬逃將賈從哲、張元經以徇。

translations.literal: Fu withdrew his troops to Lingzhou and executed the fleeing generals Jia Congzhe and Zhang Yuanjing as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Fu withdrew to Lingzhou and executed the deserters Jia Congzhe and Zhang Yuanjing as an example.

sentences.zh: 上命福佐貝勒洞鄂攻平涼。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Fu to assist Prince Dong'e in attacking Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Fu to assist Prince Dong'e in the attack on Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 福疏言固原有賊萬餘，若我兵徑趨平涼，慮賊斷我餉道，當先取固原，上韙之。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized that there were more than ten thousand rebels at Guyuan; if our army marched straight on Pingliang, he feared the rebels would cut our supply route; Guyuan should be taken first; the Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Fu argued that Guyuan held more than ten thousand rebels and that, if the army marched straight on Pingliang, the enemy might cut their supply line; Guyuan should be taken first. The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，福督兵取固原。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Fu personally directed the troops in taking Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Fu led the assault on Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 天寒大雪，士卒苦遠役，且懲前敗，有戒心。

translations.literal: The weather was bitterly cold with heavy snow; the soldiers suffered from the long campaign, and, chastened by the earlier defeat, were wary.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter cold and heavy snow afflicted the men on the long march; chastened by the earlier defeat, they were on edge.

sentences.zh: 是月甲寅朔，乙亥，師次惠安，下令：「五鼓會食，集城下，後者斬。

translations.literal: On the first day jiayin of that month, on yihai, the army halted at Hui'an; he issued the order: 'At the fifth watch assemble for food, gather below the wall; whoever comes late is to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second day of the month the army encamped at Hui'an. He ordered: 'At the fifth watch take your meal and assemble below the wall. Anyone who comes late will be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 」夜半時，參將熊虎等鼓譟入，刺福死。

translations.literal: ' At midnight, Deputy Commander Xiong Hu and others beat drums, raised a clamor, and rushed in, stabbing Fu to death.
translations.idiomatic: ' At midnight Deputy Commander Xiong Hu and others beat drums, raised a mutiny, rushed in, and stabbed Fu to death.

sentences.zh: 上以趙良棟代，收虎及首謀把總劉德及營兵戕福者悉誅之，贈福三等公，以三等精奇尼哈番世襲，諡忠愍。

translations.literal: The Emperor replaced him with Zhao Liangdong, arrested Hu and the ringleader platoon commander Liu De and all the camp soldiers who had killed Fu, and executed them all; Fu was posthumously made a third-rank duke, with third-rank Jingni Bannerman as the hereditary title, and was given the posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replaced him with Zhao Liangdong, seized Xiong Hu, the ringleader platoon commander Liu De, and all the soldiers who had killed Fu, and executed them. Fu was posthumously made a third-rank duke with a hereditary third-rank Jingni Bannerman title and given the posthumous name Zhongmin (Loyal and Sorrowful).

sentences.zh: 建祠寧夏。

translations.literal: A shrine was built for him at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial shrine was erected for him at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 擢奇天津總兵。

translations.literal: Qi was promoted to brigadier at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was promoted to brigadier at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 時福子世琳、世勳並陷賊，命以壽子世怡襲爵。

translations.literal: At that time Fu's sons Shilin and Shixun were both trapped among the rebels; the order was given that Shou's son Shiyi should inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's sons Shilin and Shixun were both trapped behind rebel lines, so Shou's son Shiyi was ordered to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 事定，壽棄官入四川求福妻子，得之遵義山中，將入都，上召世琳入見，問母子流離狀，深愍之，命襲爵，改籍寧夏。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, Shou resigned office and entered Sichuan to seek Fu's wife and children; he found them in the mountains of Zunyi; as they were about to enter the capital, the Emperor summoned Shilin for audience, asked about the mother and son's wanderings, was deeply moved with compassion, ordered him to inherit the title, and changed their registration to Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion ended, Shou resigned and went into Sichuan to find Fu's wife and children, discovering them in the hills of Zunyi. As they were about to reach the capital, the Emperor summoned Shilin, asked how mother and son had fared in exile, was deeply moved, ordered Shilin to inherit the title, and registered the family at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 旋授直隸三屯協副將。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed deputy commander of the Santun Brigade in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed deputy commander of the Santun Brigade in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 累遷古北鎮總兵、鑾儀使。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to brigadier at Gubeikou and to Director of the Imperial Procession.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to brigadier at Gubeikou and Director of the Imperial Procession.

sentences.zh: 世琳子益，益子大用，相繼襲爵。

translations.literal: Shilin's son Yi, and Yi's son Dayong, inherited the title in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Shilin's son Yi and Yi's son Dayong inherited the title in turn.

sentences.zh: 益官至楚姚鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Yi rose in office to brigadier at Chuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Yi rose to brigadier at Chuyao.

sentences.zh: 大用乾隆間官江南提督，所屬游擊楊天相，獲海盜，總督蘇凌阿讞以為誣，誅天相，大用亦被譴。

translations.literal: Dayong in the Qianlong period served as Provincial Military Commissioner of Jiangnan; his subordinate mobile battalion commander Yang Tianxiang captured pirates; Governor Su Ling'a judged the case to be a false charge, executed Tianxiang, and Dayong was also reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong, Dayong served as Provincial Military Commissioner of Jiangnan. His subordinate Yang Tianxiang captured pirates, but Governor Su Ling'a ruled the case a fabrication, had Tianxiang executed, and reprimanded Dayong as well.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，予守備銜，休致。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiaqing, he was given the brevet rank of garrison commander and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaqing he received the brevet rank of garrison commander and retired.

sentences.zh: =王之鼎=王之鼎，字公定，漢軍正紅旗人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhiding, style name Gongding, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhiding, style name Gongding, came from the Han Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 父世選，仕明為參將。

translations.literal: His father Shixuan served the Ming as a deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shixuan had served the Ming as a deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 歸太宗，授三等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: He submitted to Taizong and was granted third-rank Angbang Zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted to Taizong (Hong Taiji) and was granted third-rank Angbang Zhangjing.

sentences.zh: 從世祖入關，徵江南有功，進二等。

translations.literal: He followed Shizu in crossing the Pass, campaigned in Jiangnan with merit, and was advanced to second rank.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizu (the Shunzhi Emperor) through the Pass, earned merit in the Jiangnan campaigns, and was raised to second rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，之鼎襲，進一等精奇尼哈番，署參領。

translations.literal: When he died, Zhiding inherited, was advanced to first-rank Jingni Bannerman, and served as acting company commander.
translations.idiomatic: On his death Zhiding inherited the title, was raised to first-rank Jingni Bannerman, and served as acting company commander.

sentences.zh: 從貝勒屯齊徵湖南，擊走李定國、孫可望。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Tunqi in campaigning in Hunan and drove off Li Dingguo and Sun Kewang.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in Hunan under Prince Tunqi and drove off Li Dingguo and Sun Kewang.

sentences.zh: 授正紅旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commander of the Han Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Commander of the Han Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 駐防貴州。

translations.literal: He was stationed on garrison duty in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted on garrison duty in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，授福建中路總兵，討鄭錦，克廈門、金門、古浪諸島。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, he was appointed brigadier of the Middle Route in Fujian, campaigned against Zheng Jing, and captured Xiamen, Jinmen, Gulang, and other islands.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 (1662) he was made brigadier of Fujian's Middle Route, campaigned against Zheng Jing, and took Xiamen, Jinmen, Gulang, and other islands.

sentences.zh: 三年，敗錦將黃盛、林茂、裴德等，拔銅山衛，進三等伯。

translations.literal: In the third year, he defeated Jing's generals Huang Sheng, Lin Mao, Pei De, and others, captured Tongshan Guard, and was advanced to third-rank earl.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 (1664) he defeated Jing's generals Huang Sheng, Lin Mao, and Pei De, took Tongshan Guard, and was raised to third-rank earl.

sentences.zh: 八年，召還，仍授本旗副都統。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was recalled and again appointed Vice Commander of his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8 (1669) he was recalled and reappointed Vice Commander of his banner.

sentences.zh: 十年，授江南提督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Provincial Military Commissioner of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 10 (1671) he was appointed Provincial Military Commissioner of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授鎮海將軍，駐守京口。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was appointed Pacification-of-the-Sea General and garrisoned Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 (1673) he was made Pacification-of-the-Sea General and stationed at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂、耿精忠相繼反。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui and Geng Jingzhong rebelled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui and Geng Jingzhong rose in rebellion one after another.

sentences.zh: 上命之鼎分兵防安慶，而以安南將軍華善帥師佐之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Zhiding to detach troops to defend Anqing, while General of Annan Hua Shan led an army to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Zhiding to detach forces to defend Anqing while General of Annan Hua Shan led troops to support him.

sentences.zh: 之鼎調崇明沙船，江陰、瓜洲戰艦，扼津要，令綠旗水師駐黃浦操防，兼備水陸。

translations.literal: Zhiding deployed Chongming sand junks and warships at Jiangyin and Guazhou to hold the strategic crossings, and ordered the Green Standard naval forces to station at Huangpu for drill and defense, preparing both land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiding deployed Chongming sand junks and warships at Jiangyin and Guazhou to hold the key crossings, and stationed Green Standard naval forces at Huangpu for drill and defense, covering both land and sea.

sentences.zh: 上命簡親王喇佈為揚威大將軍，駐江寧，之鼎贊軍事。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Prince Jian Labu as Grand General for the Pacification of Insurrection, stationed at Jiangning; Zhiding assisted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor appointed Prince Jian Labu Grand General for the Pacification of Insurrection, with headquarters at Jiangning; Zhiding assisted in military planning.

sentences.zh: 十七年，改福建水師提督，加定海將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was transferred to Provincial Military Commissioner of the Fujian Naval Forces and was given the additional title of Pacification-of-Dinghai General.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 17 (1678) he was made Provincial Military Commissioner of the Fujian Naval Forces with the additional title of Pacification-of-Dinghai General.

sentences.zh: 閩寇日蹙，而楚、蜀間軍事方亟，請移鎮要地自效。

translations.literal: The Fujian rebels were daily pressed tighter, but military affairs in Chu and Shu were still urgent; he requested transfer to a key post to offer his service.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels in Fujian were daily being cornered, but fighting in Huguang and Sichuan remained fierce; he asked to be transferred to a critical post where he could serve.

sentences.zh: 十八年，調四川提督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was transferred to Provincial Military Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 (1679) he was transferred to Provincial Military Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十九年，到官，會寇犯永寧，遂率總兵李芳述等討之，戰屢勝。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, he reached his post; rebels happened to invade Yongning; he thereupon led Brigadier Li Fangshu and others to campaign against them and won repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 19 (1680) he took up his post just as rebels attacked Yongning. He led Brigadier Li Fangshu and others against them and won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 六月，勇略將軍趙良棟將進剿雲、貴，調芳述守敘州，之鼎留鎮永寧。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Valiant Strategy General Zhao Liangdong was about to advance into Yunnan and Guizhou; Fangshu was transferred to garrison Xuzhou; Zhiding remained to hold Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Valiant Strategy General Zhao Liangdong was preparing to advance into Yunnan and Guizhou. Fangshu was moved to hold Xuzhou while Zhiding remained at Yongning.

sentences.zh: 九月，吳世璠遣將尤廷玉、胡國柱攻永寧，圍之數匝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wu Shifan sent generals You Tingyu and Hu Guozhu to attack Yongning and surrounded it in many rings.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wu Shifan sent generals You Tingyu and Hu Guozhu against Yongning and invested the city in tight rings.

sentences.zh: 時城中糧盡已兩閱月，之鼎猶率兵挑戰，士氣倍奮。

translations.literal: At that time grain in the city had been exhausted for two months, yet Zhiding still led the troops out to offer battle, and morale was doubly roused.
translations.idiomatic: Grain in the city had been gone for two months, yet Zhiding still led sorties against the enemy, and the troops' spirit doubled.

sentences.zh: 嗣為賊诇知，築長圍以守。

translations.literal: Afterward the rebels learned this by reconnaissance and built a long encirclement to hold their position.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels learned of this through scouts, they built a long encirclement and settled in to wait.

sentences.zh: 至是月甲子，寇穴城入，總兵費雅達，副將楊三虎，游擊週尚功，守備李逢春、魯明芝、席豹督兵巷戰，皆死。

translations.literal: On jiazi of that month, the rebels tunneled into the city; Brigadier Fei Yada, Deputy Commander Yang Sanhu, Mobile Battalion Commander Zhou Shanggong, and Garrison Commanders Li Fengchun, Lu Mingzhi, and Xi Bao personally directed troops in street fighting and all died.
translations.idiomatic: On that month's jiazi day the rebels tunneled into the city. Brigadier Fei Yada, Deputy Commander Yang Sanhu, Mobile Battalion Commander Zhou Shanggong, and Garrison Commanders Li Fengchun, Lu Mingzhi, and Xi Bao led street fighting and all fell.

sentences.zh: 之鼎解印付家人，令間道走成都，率總兵楊魁、何成德、王永世、傅汝友，游擊陳先鳳、陳田、劉應科等出禦賊，身受重創。

translations.literal: Zhiding removed his seal and gave it to his household, ordering them to take a bypath and flee to Chengdu; he led Brigadiers Yang Kui, He Chengde, Wang Yongshi, and Fu Ruyou, and Mobile Battalion Commanders Chen Xianfeng, Chen Tian, and Liu Yingke, and others out to meet the rebels and was himself severely wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiding handed his seal to his household and told them to escape by a hidden route to Chengdu. He led Brigadiers Yang Kui, He Chengde, Wang Yongshi, and Fu Ruyou and Mobile Battalion Commanders Chen Xianfeng, Chen Tian, and Liu Yingke out to face the enemy and was gravely wounded.

sentences.zh: 賊湧至，之鼎自度不能免，拔劍自刎，未殊，與魁等俱被執，傳送貴陽。

translations.literal: The rebels surged up; Zhiding judged that he could not escape, drew his sword and cut his throat, but was not yet dead; he and Kui and the others were all seized and sent under escort to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels swarmed in. Seeing no escape, Zhiding drew his sword and cut his throat but did not die outright. He and Kui and the others were captured and sent to Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 賊黨夏國相等百計誘降，之鼎厲聲叱曰：「死則死耳，肯向鼠輩乞活耶？

translations.literal: The rebel partisan Xia Guoxiang and others used every stratagem to entice him to surrender; Zhiding rebuked them in a stern voice, saying: 'To die is to die—would I beg life from such vermin?
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders such as Xia Guoxiang tried every means to win him over. Zhiding shouted back: 'Death is death—would I beg my life from vermin like you?

sentences.zh: 」久之，賊知不可奪，遂遇害。

translations.literal: ' After a long time, the rebels knew he could not be won over and thereupon put him to death.
translations.idiomatic: ' In time the rebels saw he could not be turned and killed him.

sentences.zh: 魁等皆不屈死。

translations.literal: Kui and the others all died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Kui and the others likewise refused to submit and were killed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈之鼎太子少保，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Zhiding was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhongyi (Loyal and Resolute).
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Zhiding was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhongyi (Loyal and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 子毓賢，官至貴州布政使，毓秀襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yuxian rose in office to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guizhou; Yuxiu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuxian rose to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guizhou; Yuxiu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: =費雅達=費雅達，漢軍正白旗人。

translations.literal: Fei Yada was a Han Bannerman of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yada came from the Han Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 自整儀尉累遷潼關副將。

translations.literal: From Ceremonial Guard he was promoted repeatedly until he became deputy commander at Tongguan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Ceremonial Guard through successive posts to deputy commander at Tongguan.

sentences.zh: 王輔臣叛，廷議設漢中總兵討賊，以授費雅達，署都督僉事。

translations.literal: When Wang Fuchen rebelled, the court debated establishing a brigadier at Hanzhong to campaign against the rebels and appointed Fei Yada, with the acting rank of Regional Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Fuchen rebelled, the court decided to create a Hanzhong brigadier to fight the rebels and gave the post to Fei Yada with the acting rank of Regional Vice Commander.

sentences.zh: 進取漢中，破賊彝門鎮，抵秦嶺，拔北木城，與王進寶會師奪武關。

translations.literal: He advanced to take Hanzhong, defeated the rebels at Yimen Town, reached the Qin Mountains, captured Beimu Fort, joined forces with Wang Jinbao, and together recovered Wuguan.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Hanzhong, broke the rebels at Yimen Town, reached the Qin Mountains, took Beimu Fort, and joined Wang Jinbao to recover Wuguan.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加都督同知。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was given the rank of Regional Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Regional Vice Commander.

sentences.zh: 永寧之役，城陷身死，贈左都督、太子少傅，諡忠勇。

translations.literal: In the Yongning campaign, when the city fell he died in the fighting; he was posthumously made Left Regional Commander and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhongyong (Loyal and Valiant).
translations.idiomatic: At Yongning the city fell and he died in battle. He was posthumously made Left Regional Commander and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhongyong (Loyal and Valiant).

sentences.zh: 魁等皆予卹。

translations.literal: Kui and the others were all granted funeral honors.
translations.idiomatic: Kui and the others likewise received funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 從三虎等戰死者，又有千總蔣得福、趙鳴鳳、王英傑；

translations.literal: Among those who died fighting with Sanhu were also Battalion Commanders Jiang Defu, Zhao Mingfeng, and Wang Yingjie;
translations.idiomatic: Those who fell fighting with Sanhu also included Battalion Commanders Jiang Defu, Zhao Mingfeng, and Wang Yingjie;

sentences.zh: 從之鼎死者，又有從軍廕生潘濟世：並卹如例。

translations.literal: among those who died with Zhiding was also the military student by enfeoffment Pan Jishi: all received funeral honors according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: among those who died with Zhiding was also the enfeoffed military student Pan Jishi; all received funeral honors according to precedent.

sentences.zh: =李興元=李興元，字若始，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Li Xingyuan, style name Ruoshi, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingyuan, style name Ruoshi, came from the Han Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 以拔貢授直隸沙河知縣，報最，遷祁州。

translations.literal: Through the special examination for tribute students he was appointed magistrate of Shahe in Zhili; his administration was rated highest and he was transferred to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Selected through the tribute examination, he was appointed magistrate of Shahe in Zhili. Rated highest in his review, he was moved to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 歷江西吉安、直隸永平知府，晉陝西隴右道。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Ji'an in Jiangxi and Yongping in Zhili, and was promoted to Longyou Circuit Intendant in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Ji'an in Jiangxi and Yongping in Zhili, then rose to Longyou Circuit Intendant in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年，授雲南按察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi, he was appointed Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11 (1672) he was appointed Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 其明年，詔敕有司審理平西籓下逃兵。

translations.literal: The next year, an edict ordered the officials to try and judge deserters from the Pacification of the West fief.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict ordered officials to try deserters from Wu Sangui's Pacification of the West fief.

sentences.zh: 時平西勳莊棋布，管莊者殺人奪貨，滋為民患。

translations.literal: At that time the merit estates of the Pacification of the West were spread about like chess pieces; those who managed the estates killed people and seized goods, becoming a growing affliction on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's merit estates were scattered across the province like chess pieces. Estate managers killed and plundered, becoming a growing scourge on the people.

sentences.zh: 訟牒命、盜兩案，兵居半。

translations.literal: In cases of murder and robbery on the dockets, soldiers made up half.
translations.idiomatic: Murder and robbery cases filled the dockets, and soldiers accounted for half of them.

sentences.zh: 又勒平民為餘丁；

translations.literal: They also forced commoners to serve as surplus soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: They also forced commoners to register as surplus soldiers;

sentences.zh: 不從，則曰：「是我逃兵也。

translations.literal: if they refused, they would say: 'These are my deserters.
translations.idiomatic: and if anyone refused they would say, 'These are my deserters.

sentences.zh: 」稱貸重息，人或絲毫負，亦以「逃兵」誣之，有司亡誰何。

translations.literal: ' They lent money at heavy interest, and if someone owed even the slightest amount, they would also falsely accuse him of being a 'deserter'; the officials had no one to hold accountable.
translations.idiomatic: ' They lent at crushing interest, and even a trifling debt could be branded as 'desertion.' Officials dared not hold them accountable.

sentences.zh: 興元素持風力，諗知劉昆強項，令為審事官。

translations.literal: Xingyuan had always been firm in character; knowing that Liu Kun was a tough-minded man, he appointed him reviewing officer.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan was known for his firm character. Knowing Liu Kun to be tough-minded, he made him reviewing officer.

sentences.zh: 有犯者論如法，部民德之，而大忤三桂意。

translations.literal: When offenders were judged according to law, the people of the department were grateful to him, but this greatly offended Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders were punished according to law, to the people's gratitude, but this deeply offended Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 三桂將叛，使冶者鑄印，昆诇知，白興元，興元啟巡撫硃國治，趣入告。

translations.literal: When Sangui was about to rebel, he had a metalworker cast seals; Kun learned of this by reconnaissance and reported to Xingyuan; Xingyuan informed Governor Zhu Guozhi and urged him to report quickly to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As Wu Sangui prepared to rebel, he had seals cast. Kun discovered this through reconnaissance and told Xingyuan, who alerted Governor Zhu Guozhi and urged him to report at once to the capital.

sentences.zh: 國治遲數日始發，為三桂邏卒所得，遂作亂。

translations.literal: Guozhi delayed several days before sending the report; it was seized by Sangui's courier troops, and rebellion followed.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhi delayed several days before dispatching the report. Sangui's couriers seized it, and rebellion followed.

sentences.zh: 召各官集議，以國治苛虐失民心，殺之；

translations.literal: He summoned the officials to assemble for deliberation, saying that because Guozhi was harsh and cruel and had lost the people's hearts, he should be killed;
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the officials and, claiming Guozhi's harsh rule had lost the people's hearts, had him killed;

sentences.zh: 迫授興元偽職，興元叱之曰：「汝內為國戚，外封親王，受恩重矣，何叛為？

translations.literal: he forced Xingyuan to accept a false office; Xingyuan rebuked him, saying: 'Within you are the Emperor's kin by marriage; without you are enfeoffed as a prince—your grace has been great; why rebel?
translations.idiomatic: and tried to force a false office on Xingyuan. Xingyuan rebuked him: 'You are the Emperor's kin by marriage and enfeoffed as a prince—the grace shown you has been great. Why rebel?

sentences.zh: 我為丈夫，義可殺不可辱，惟一死以報朝廷。

translations.literal: I am a man; righteousness permits death but not disgrace; I have only death with which to repay the court.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of honor. Righteousness allows death but not disgrace. I have only my death to offer the court.

sentences.zh: 」三桂怒，杖而下之獄。

translations.literal: ' Sangui in anger had him beaten and cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: ' Wu Sangui in anger had him beaten and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 雲南知府高顯辰及昆皆不屈，旋以興元及昆戍騰越衛。

translations.literal: Yunnan Prefect Gao Xianchen and Kun likewise would not yield; shortly afterward Xingyuan and Kun were sent under guard to Tengyue Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan Prefect Gao Xianchen and Kun likewise refused to submit. Soon Xingyuan and Kun were sent under guard to Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 十八年，師克湖南，時三桂已死，其子世璠使刺殺興元。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the army captured Hunan, Sangui was already dead; his son Shifan sent assassins to kill Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 (1679), as government forces took Hunan, Wu Sangui was already dead. His son Shifan sent assassins to kill Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 師困滇城，興元二子廕秀、奇秀亦被殺。

translations.literal: When the army besieged the city of Yunnan, Xingyuan's two sons, the enfeoffed Xiuxiu and Qixiu, were also killed.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Yunnan, Xingyuan's enfeoffed sons Xiuxiu and Qixiu were also killed.

sentences.zh: 事定，其三子萃秀詣軍所申訴，巡撫王繼文上其狀，贈太常寺卿。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, his third son Cuixiu went to the army camp to lodge a complaint; Governor Wang Jiwen reported the facts, and Xingyuan was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion ended, his third son Cuixiu appealed at army headquarters. Governor Wang Jiwen reported the case, and Xingyuan was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 萃秀官至安陸府知府。

translations.literal: Cuixiu rose in office to prefect of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Cuixiu rose to prefect of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 昆當興元未死，出避民間。

translations.literal: While Xingyuan had not yet died, Kun went out and hid among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xingyuan died, Kun went into hiding among the people.

sentences.zh: 事定，复補登州同知，遷常德知府。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he was again appointed acting subprefect of Dengzhou and was transferred to prefect of Changde.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion he was reappointed acting subprefect of Dengzhou and later made prefect of Changde.

sentences.zh: =陳啟泰=陳啟泰，字大來，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Chen Qitai, style name Dalai, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qitai, style name Dalai, came from the Han Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，自貢生知直隸滑縣，有聲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, through the tribute student examination he was appointed magistrate of Huaxian in Zhili and gained a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4 (1647) he passed the tribute examination and was appointed magistrate of Huaxian in Zhili, where he earned a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 行取，擢御史。

translations.literal: Through special selection he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Through special selection he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「滿洲部院官凡遇親喪，宜離任守制，以廣孝治。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: 'Whenever Manchu officials of the boards and departments encounter a parent's death, they should leave office to observe mourning, thereby extending the rule of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: 'When Manchu officials of the boards and departments suffer a parent's death, they should leave office to observe mourning, thereby extending the rule of filial piety.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ' The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: ' The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十一年，出為蘇松糧道。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he went out to serve as Grain Intendant of Suzhou and Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11 (1672) he was made Grain Intendant of Suzhou and Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，調福建漳南道。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi, he was transferred to Zhangnan Circuit in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 (1664) he was transferred to Zhangnan Circuit in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉巡海道。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred to Coastal Patrol Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8 (1669) he was made Coastal Patrol Circuit Intendant.

sentences.zh: 時山寇遍受耿精忠劄，勢洶洶。

translations.literal: At that time mountain bandits everywhere received commissions from Geng Jingzhong, and their power was menacing.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain bandits throughout the region were taking commissions from Geng Jingzhong, and their power grew menacing.

sentences.zh: 啟泰嚴保甲，立團長，親督所司捕賊。

translations.literal: Qitai strictly enforced the baojia system, established group leaders, and personally supervised his subordinates in capturing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Qitai strictly enforced the baojia system, appointed group leaders, and personally supervised the capture of bandits.

sentences.zh: 有乾禁令者，輒痛繩以法，姦宄屏息。

translations.literal: Whoever violated the prohibition was sternly punished by law, and evildoers fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Violators were sternly punished by law until evildoers fell silent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，精忠叛，偽檄至漳州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Jingzhong rebelled and a false proclamation reached Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 (1674) Jingzhong rebelled and a false proclamation reached Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 啟泰密與海澄公黃梧議拒守，會梧病，精忠复招鄭錦為助。

translations.literal: Qitai secretly discussed resistance with Duke of Haicheng Huang Wu, but Wu fell ill; Jingzhong again recruited Zheng Jing as aid.
translations.idiomatic: Qitai secretly planned resistance with Duke of Haicheng Huang Wu, but Wu fell ill. Jingzhong then recruited Zheng Jing as ally.

sentences.zh: 啟泰自度不能守，語妻劉曰：「義不偷生，忠不附賊，死吾事也。

translations.literal: Qitai judged that he could not hold the city and said to his wife Liu: 'Righteousness forbids living in disgrace; loyalty forbids joining rebels—death is my duty.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not hold the city, Qitai told his wife Liu: 'Righteousness forbids living in disgrace; loyalty forbids joining rebels. Death is my duty.

sentences.zh: 然死而妻子為僇，吾何以瞑？

translations.literal: Yet if I die and my wife and children are slaughtered, how can I close my eyes?
translations.idiomatic: But if I die and my wife and children are slaughtered, how can I rest?

sentences.zh: 」劉請殉，家人皆原從死。

translations.literal: ' Liu asked to die with him, and the household all wished to follow.
translations.idiomatic: ' Liu asked to die with him, and the whole household wished to follow.

sentences.zh: 乃以巨盎置酒下藥，劉及侍妾婢僕飲者二十一人。

translations.literal: They therefore placed a great basin, poured wine, and added poison; Liu and twenty serving women and maids who drank numbered twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: They set out a great basin of wine laced with poison. Liu and twenty-one servants and maids who drank included

sentences.zh: 幼子方六歲，持觴拜而飲。

translations.literal: His youngest son, only six years old, took the cup, bowed, and drank.
translations.idiomatic: his six-year-old son, who took the cup, bowed, and drank.

sentences.zh: 啟泰朝服坐堂皇，召僚屬與訣，引弓弦自絞死，僚屬為殯。

translations.literal: Qitai in court dress sat in the main hall, summoned his subordinates to bid farewell, drew a bowstring and strangled himself to death; the subordinates prepared his burial.
translations.idiomatic: Qitai in court dress sat in the main hall, bade his subordinates farewell, and strangled himself with a bowstring. His subordinates prepared his burial.

sentences.zh: 錦兵入，見置棺縱橫，皆垂淚。

translations.literal: When Jing's troops entered, they saw coffins set out in rows and all wept.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Jing's troops entered, they saw rows of coffins and wept.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈通政使，賜葬祭。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Qitai was posthumously made Commissioner of the Court of State Ceremonial and granted sacrificial burial.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Qitai was posthumously made Commissioner of the Court of State Ceremonial and granted sacrificial burial.

sentences.zh: 啟泰子汝器，聞變，赴漳州迎喪，為鄭錦兵掠去。

translations.literal: Qitai's son Ruqi, on hearing of the disaster, went to Zhangzhou to meet the funeral procession and was seized by Zheng Jing's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Qitai's son Ruqi, hearing of the disaster, went to Zhangzhou to meet the funeral train and was seized by Zheng Jing's troops.

sentences.zh: 逾二年乃脫還，詣京師，上念其父子忠義，加贈工部侍郎，授汝器右通政。

translations.literal: Only after more than two years did he escape and return; he went to the capital, and the Emperor, mindful of the father and son's loyalty, additionally posthumously made Qitai Vice Minister of the Board of Works and appointed Ruqi Right Vice Commissioner of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: After more than two years he escaped and reached the capital. Mindful of the father and son's loyalty, the Emperor additionally posthumously made Qitai Vice Minister of the Board of Works and appointed Ruqi Right Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，复予啟泰諡忠毅。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, Qitai was again given the posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 33 (1694) Qitai was again given the posthumous title Zhongyi (Loyal and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 建祠福州，御書「忠義流芳」為祠額。

translations.literal: A shrine was built at Fuzhou, and the Emperor personally wrote 'Loyalty and Righteousness Flow Forever' as the shrine inscription.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was built at Fuzhou, with the imperial inscription 'Loyalty and Righteousness Flow Forever.'

sentences.zh: 汝器官至安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Ruqi rose in office to Governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Ruqi rose to Governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 方精忠叛時，諸郡望風納叛；

translations.literal: When Jingzhong rebelled, the prefectures for the most part surrendered at his approach;
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhong rebelled, most prefectures surrendered at his approach;

sentences.zh: 所不肯以城降者，啟泰死漳州，總兵吳萬福死福寧。

translations.literal: those who would not surrender their cities were Qitai, who died at Zhangzhou, and Brigadier Wu Wanfu, who died at Funing.
translations.idiomatic: those who refused to surrender were Qitai at Zhangzhou and Brigadier Wu Wanfu at Funing.

sentences.zh: 萬福，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Wanfu was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wanfu came from the Han Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 初仕明為守備。

translations.literal: He first served the Ming as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served the Ming as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 崇德七年，師圍松山，從副將夏承德來歸，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongde, when the army besieged Songshan, he came over with Deputy Commander Xia Chengde and was appointed company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 7 (1642), when the army besieged Songshan, he came over with Deputy Commander Xia Chengde and was made company commander.

sentences.zh: 入關，從征李自成有功，累敘二等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: After crossing the Pass, he followed the campaign against Li Zicheng with merit and was repeatedly recorded for second-rank Adaha Bannerman.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Pass he earned merit against Li Zicheng and was repeatedly recorded for second-rank Adaha Bannerman.

sentences.zh: 出為福寧總兵。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as brigadier at Funing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed brigadier at Funing.

sentences.zh: 張煌言兵屢入，與總兵李長榮分路擊卻之，累進右都督，精忠叛，萬福嬰城固守，城破，死之，闔家被害。

translations.literal: Zhang Huangyan's troops repeatedly entered; together with Brigadier Li Changrong he drove them off by separate routes, was repeatedly advanced to Right Regional Commander; when Jingzhong rebelled, Wanfu defended the city with a closed garrison; when the city fell he died, and his whole family was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huangyan's forces raided repeatedly; with Brigadier Li Changrong he beat them back along separate routes and rose to Right Regional Commander. When Jingzhong rebelled, Wanfu held Funing in a closed defense; when the city fell he died and his whole family perished.

sentences.zh: 幕客孫墢、百總潘騰鳳並殉。

translations.literal: His secretary Sun Kan and company commander Pan Tengfeng also died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His secretary Sun Kan and company commander Pan Tengfeng died with him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈萬福左都督、太子少保，諡忠愍。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Wanfu was posthumously made Left Regional Commander and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Wanfu was posthumously made Left Regional Commander and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhongmin (Loyal and Sorrowful).

sentences.zh: =陳丹赤=陳丹赤，字獻之，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: Chen Danchi, style name Xianzhi, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Danchi, style name Xianzhi, came from Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 順治十七年舉人，選授重慶推官，攝府事，兼署夔州府。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi he passed the provincial examination; he was selected and appointed reviewing officer at Chongqing, acting in prefectural affairs and concurrently acting prefect of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17 (1660) he passed the provincial examination and was appointed reviewing officer at Chongqing, acting for the prefect and concurrently for Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 時張獻忠初滅，蜀東尚淪於賊，徵師四集，丹赤給餉不乏。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Xianzhong had just been destroyed; eastern Shu was still overrun by bandits, and expeditionary armies gathered on all sides; Danchi supplied provisions without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong had just been destroyed, eastern Sichuan was still overrun, and expeditionary armies gathered on all sides, yet Danchi kept provisions flowing without fail.

sentences.zh: 墾荒萊，緩刑禁，報最，遷刑部主事，再晉兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He opened wasteland, eased penal restrictions, his administration was rated highest, he was transferred to a secretary in the Board of Punishments, and was again promoted to director in the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: He opened wasteland, eased penal restrictions, earned the highest rating, was moved to secretary in the Board of Punishments, and then to director in the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 出為浙江按察司僉事、分巡溫處道，署按察使。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang and Circuit Intendant of Wenzhou and Chuzhou, acting as Provincial Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang and Circuit Intendant of Wenzhou and Chuzhou, acting as Provincial Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，入覲，道山東。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, he came to court for audience by way of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 (1674) he came to court for audience by way of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 會吳三桂反，詔入覲官悉還治所。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui happened to rebel; an edict ordered all officials coming to audience to return to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui rebelled just then, and an edict ordered all officials en route to audience to return to their posts.

sentences.zh: 丹赤歸至東昌，聞耿精忠亦叛，亟間道還。

translations.literal: Danchi returned as far as Dongchang; hearing that Geng Jingzhong had also rebelled, he hurried back by a hidden route.
translations.idiomatic: Danchi reached Dongchang, heard that Geng Jingzhong had rebelled too, and hurried back by a hidden route.

sentences.zh: 適平陽叛將司定猷構精忠兵偪瑞安，丹赤獨居城上，泣諭父老，誓與城存亡。

translations.literal: Pingyang rebel general Si Dingyou had joined with Jingzhong's troops to press on Ruian; Danchi alone stood on the city wall, weeping as he addressed the elders, and swore to live or die with the city.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang rebel Si Dingyou had joined Jingzhong's forces against Ruian. Danchi stood alone on the wall, weeping as he addressed the elders and swore to live or die with the city.

sentences.zh: 海寇硃飛熊乘間肆掠，鄉民爭入城，總兵祖弘勳慾不納。

translations.literal: Sea bandit Zhu Feixiong took advantage of the disorder to plunder; the villagers all rushed into the city, but Brigadier Zu Hongxun wished not to admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Sea bandit Zhu Feixiong plundered amid the chaos. Villagers rushed into the city, but Brigadier Zu Hongxun wished to shut them out.

sentences.zh: 丹赤曰：「城以人為固，人以食為命。

translations.literal: Danchi said: 'A city is made firm by its people; people live by food.
translations.idiomatic: Danchi said: 'A city stands firm through its people, and people live by food.

sentences.zh: 民輦粟入城，民即兵，食即餉。

translations.literal: When the people bring grain into the city, the people become soldiers and food becomes pay.
translations.idiomatic: When people bring grain into the city, the people become soldiers and food becomes pay.

sentences.zh: 亟宜納之，與共守。

translations.literal: They should be admitted at once and defended together.
translations.idiomatic: Admit them at once and defend together.

sentences.zh: 」於是來者數万。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon those who came numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: ' Tens of thousands then entered.

sentences.zh: 寇湧至，攻南門甚亟，副將楊春芳忽撤兵去，人心洶懼。

translations.literal: The rebels surged up and attacked the south gate fiercely; Deputy Commander Yang Chunfang suddenly withdrew his troops, and popular feeling was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels surged against the south gate. Deputy Commander Yang Chunfang suddenly withdrew, and panic spread.

sentences.zh: 丹赤日馳牒乞援，晨夜徼循，以忠義厲士卒，皆感泣，願死守。

translations.literal: Danchi daily sent urgent dispatches begging for relief, patrolled morning and night, and roused the troops with talk of loyalty and righteousness; all were moved to tears and wished to die defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: Danchi sent daily pleas for relief, patrolled day and night, and stirred the troops with loyalty and righteousness until all wept and vowed to die defending the city.

sentences.zh: 弘勳將以溫州叛，陽遣游擊馬文始助守，實以诇丹赤，丹赤誓以身殉。

translations.literal: Hongxun was about to surrender Wenzhou and pretended to send Mobile Battalion Commander Ma Wenshi to help defend, but in fact used him to spy on Danchi; Danchi swore to die for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxun planned to surrender Wenzhou and pretended to send Mobile Battalion Commander Ma Wenshi to help defend while using him to spy on Danchi. Danchi swore to die for the cause.

sentences.zh: 六月甲午朔，弘勳陳甲仗華蓋山，集文武官計事，欲以脅丹赤。

translations.literal: On the first day jiawu of the sixth month, Hongxun arrayed arms and armor at Huagai Mountain and gathered civil and military officials to deliberate, intending to coerce Danchi.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month Hongxun arrayed arms at Huagai Mountain and gathered officials, intending to coerce Danchi.

sentences.zh: 千總姚紹英知其謀，勸勿往，丹赤不顧，策馬去。

translations.literal: Battalion Commander Yao Shaoying learned of the plot and urged him not to go; Danchi paid no heed and rode off.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion Commander Yao Shaoying learned of the plot and urged him not to go. Danchi ignored him and rode off.

sentences.zh: 至則兵露刃夾階立，坐定，弘勳曰：「彼眾我寡，將若何？

translations.literal: When he arrived, soldiers with bared blades stood on both sides of the steps; when he was seated, Hongxun said: 'They are many and we are few—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers with bared blades lined the steps. When seated, Hongxun said: 'They are many and we are few. What shall we do?

sentences.zh: 」丹赤曰：「提標前鋒五千人已集，且民心效死，戰即不足，守自有餘。

translations.literal: ' Danchi said: 'The commander's vanguard of five thousand men has already assembled, and moreover the people's hearts are set on dying in defense; if fighting is insufficient, holding the city will be enough.
translations.idiomatic: ' Danchi said: 'Five thousand vanguard troops have already assembled, and the people are ready to die in defense. If we cannot fight, we can still hold.

sentences.zh: 吾此來商以舟濟師，顧乃計多寡邪？

translations.literal: I came here to discuss ferrying troops by boat—yet you speak of numbers?
translations.idiomatic: I came to discuss ferrying troops by boat—yet you count heads?

sentences.zh: 」弘勳曰：「舟安在？

translations.literal: ' Hongxun said: 'Where are the boats?
translations.idiomatic: ' Hongxun said: 'Where are the boats?

sentences.zh: 」丹赤語通判白鼇宸曰：「河干泊舟不少，皆鄉民所棄。

translations.literal: ' Danchi said to Acting Prefect Bai Aichen: 'Many boats are moored along the riverbank—all abandoned by the villagers.
translations.idiomatic: ' Danchi told Acting Prefect Bai Aichen: 'Many boats lie along the riverbank, abandoned by the villagers.

sentences.zh: 以濟援師，何患無舟？

translations.literal: Use them to ferry relief troops—why fear there are no boats?
translations.idiomatic: Use them to ferry relief troops. What lack of boats?

sentences.zh: 」弘勳語塞，春芳厲聲言曰：「城中糧盡，縱有兵有舟，誰為我用？

translations.literal: ' Hongxun was left speechless; Chunfang said in a harsh voice: 'Grain in the city is exhausted; even if there were troops and boats, who would fight for us?
translations.idiomatic: ' Hongxun was speechless. Chunfang said harshly: 'Grain in the city is gone. Even with troops and boats, who would fight for us?

sentences.zh: 」丹赤曰：「若言誤矣。

translations.literal: ' Danchi said: 'You speak wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: ' Danchi said: 'You are mistaken.

sentences.zh: 吾軍糧餉足供六閱月，且遠近鄉民輸粟入。

translations.literal: Our army's grain and pay are sufficient for six months, and moreover villagers near and far are bringing grain in.
translations.idiomatic: Our grain and pay will last six months, and villagers near and far are still bringing grain in.

sentences.zh: 若乃為此言惑軍心邪？

translations.literal: Are you trying to confuse the army's hearts with such talk?
translations.idiomatic: Are you trying to shake the army's hearts?

sentences.zh: 」有自懷中出帛書者，精忠招弘勳獻城檄也，丹赤怒，碎而擲之地，曰：「此豈可污吾目？

translations.literal: ' Someone produced a silk letter from his bosom—the proclamation by which Jingzhong recruited Hongxun to surrender the city; Danchi in anger tore it to pieces and threw it on the ground, saying: 'How can this defile my eyes?
translations.idiomatic: ' Someone produced from his bosom Jingzhong's proclamation recruiting Hongxun to surrender the city. Danchi tore it to pieces and threw it down: 'How can this defile my eyes?

sentences.zh: 吾頭可斷，城不可得也！

translations.literal: My head may be cut off, but the city will not be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: My head may fall, but the city will not be taken!

sentences.zh: 」弘勳執其手，好語慰之，丹赤曰：「封疆之臣死封疆，不知其他。

translations.literal: ' Hongxun took his hand and spoke soothing words; Danchi said: 'A frontier official dies on the frontier—I know nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: ' Hongxun took his hand and spoke soothingly. Danchi said: 'A frontier official dies on the frontier. I know nothing else.

sentences.zh: 」弘勳知不可奪，目千總高魁持斧擁丹赤出，罵益厲，執斧者斷其臂，大呼曰：「臣事畢矣！

translations.literal: ' Hongxun knew he could not be won over; he signaled Battalion Commander Gao Kui, who with an axe escorted Danchi out; Danchi cursed all the more fiercely; the man with the axe cut off his arm, and he cried out loudly: 'My duty as a minister is finished!
translations.idiomatic: ' Hongxun saw he could not be turned. He signaled Battalion Commander Gao Kui, who with an axe escorted Danchi out. Danchi cursed all the louder. The axeman cut off his arm, and he cried: 'My duty as a minister is finished!

sentences.zh: 」兵刃交下，遂遇害。

translations.literal: ' Blades crossed and he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: ' Blades fell on him and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 十六年，浙江巡撫陳秉直疏請卹，贈通政使，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Zhejiang Governor Chen Bingzhi memorialized requesting funeral honors; Danchi was posthumously made Commissioner of the Court of State Ceremonial, with the posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 (1677) Zhejiang Governor Chen Bingzhi asked for funeral honors. Danchi was posthumously made Commissioner of the Court of State Ceremonial with the posthumous title Zhongyi (Loyal and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 三十八年，上南巡，丹赤子一夔時為湖州知府，迎謁，上書額賜之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, when the Emperor made a southern tour, Danchi's son Yiqi was then prefect of Huzhou; he came to pay respects, and the Emperor wrote an inscription and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 38 (1699), during the southern tour, Danchi's son Yiqi, then prefect of Huzhou, came to pay respects and received an imperial inscription.

sentences.zh: =馬閟=馬閟，字奉璋，陝西武功人。

translations.literal: Ma Bi, style name Fengzhang, was a native of Wugong in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Bi, style name Fengzhang, came from Wugong in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年舉人，授山東昌樂知縣，有惠政。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi he passed the provincial examination; he was appointed magistrate of Changle in Shandong and had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 (1654) he passed the provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Changle in Shandong, where he governed with benevolence.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，補永嘉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, he was appointed to Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 (1674) he was appointed to Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 明決有才，清覈圖籍，不數月而政成。

translations.literal: He was clear and decisive and talented; he examined the registers thoroughly, and within a few months his administration was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Clear and decisive, he audited the registers thoroughly and brought order within months.

sentences.zh: 華蓋山集議，弘勳戕丹赤，閟躍而起曰：「國家豢若輩，反黨賊殺封疆大吏，吾恥與若輩俱生！

translations.literal: At the assembly on Huagai Mountain, when Hongxun killed Danchi, Bi leaped up and said: 'The state has nurtured you, yet you turn bandit and kill a frontier grand official—I am ashamed to live with you!
translations.idiomatic: At the Huagai Mountain assembly, when Hongxun killed Danchi, Bi leaped up and cried: 'The state nurtured you, yet you join rebels and murder a frontier minister. I am ashamed to live among you!

sentences.zh: 」遂罵不絕口，同時遇害。

translations.literal: ' He cursed without cease and was killed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: ' He cursed without cease and was killed with the rest.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈布政司參政。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously made Assistant Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously made Assistant Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，敕建祠溫州，祀丹赤及閟，亦曰「雙忠」。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, an edict ordered a shrine built at Wenzhou to sacrifice to Danchi and Bi, also called 'Twin Loyalty.'
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35 (1696) an edict ordered a shrine at Wenzhou for Danchi and Bi, called 'Twin Loyalty.'

sentences.zh: 四十二年，上南巡，閟子逸姿官江南布政司參議督糧道，迎謁，疏引丹赤例求賜諡，上允之，諡忠勤，亦賜御書額如一夔。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, when the Emperor made a southern tour, Bi's son Yizi was Assistant Provincial Administration Commissioner in charge of grain transport in Jiangnan; he came to pay respects and memorialized citing Danchi's precedent to request a posthumous title; the Emperor approved, giving the title Zhongqin, and also bestowed an imperial inscription as to Yiqi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 42 (1703), during the southern tour, Bi's son Yizi, then grain transport commissioner in Jiangnan, cited Danchi's precedent and received the posthumous title Zhongqin (Loyal and Diligent), with an imperial inscription like Yiqi's.

sentences.zh: 丹赤役林莪、僕張亦寶，閟從子穎姿，皆從死。

translations.literal: Danchi's laborer Lin E, servant Zhang Yibao, and Bi's nephew Yingzi all followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: Danchi's laborer Lin E, servant Zhang Yibao, and Bi's nephew Yingzi all died with them.

sentences.zh: =葉映榴=葉映榴，字炳霞，江南上海人。

translations.literal: Ye Yingliu, style name Bingxia, was a native of Shanghai in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yingliu, style name Bingxia, came from Shanghai in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治十八年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Shunzhi he passed the palace examination and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 18 (1661) he passed the palace examination and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 時方嚴治江南逋賦士紳，映榴在籍中，降國子監博士。

translations.literal: At that time the court was strictly punishing gentry in Jiangnan for tax arrears; Yingliu was on the register and was demoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then strictly punishing Jiangnan gentry for tax arrears. Yingliu was on the list and was demoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to director in the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to director in the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出榷贛關，會吳三桂叛，贛南北路絕。

translations.literal: He went out to supervise the Ganzhou customs station; Wu Sangui happened to rebel, and the northern and southern routes through Ganzhou were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He went to supervise the Ganzhou customs station. When Wu Sangui rebelled, routes north and south through Ganzhou were cut.

sentences.zh: 映榴與同官守險要，撫流民，境獲寧。

translations.literal: Yingliu and his colleagues held the strategic passes, pacified displaced people, and the region was brought to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yingliu and his colleagues held the strategic passes, pacified refugees, and restored peace to the region.

sentences.zh: 提學陝西巡撫鄂愷薦其才，康熙二十四年，授湖廣糧儲道。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Education Commissioner and Governor E Kai recommended his talent; in the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi, he was appointed Grain Storage Intendant of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Education Commissioner and Governor E Kai recommended him. In Kangxi 24 (1685) he was appointed Grain Storage Intendant of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 清積逋，減耗羨，事有不便於民者，輒與大吏力爭。

translations.literal: He cleared long-standing arrears, reduced meltage surcharges, and whenever something was harmful to the people he vigorously disputed it with the grand officials.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared long-standing arrears, reduced meltage surcharges, and whenever a policy harmed the people he argued fiercely with the senior officials.

sentences.zh: 二十七年五月，廷議省湖廣總督，並裁督標兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-seventh year, the court debated abolishing the Governor-General of Huguang and also disbanding the governor's personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kangxi 27 (1688) the court debated abolishing the Huguang Governor-General and disbanding his personal troops.

sentences.zh: 楚兵素剽悍，有夏逢龍者，尤桀黠，能以小信義結其伍，隱附之。

translations.literal: The Chu troops had always been fierce; among them Xia Fenglong was especially cunning and could bind his comrades with small acts of trust, secretly gathering followers.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang troops had always been fierce. Xia Fenglong was especially cunning and won followers with small acts of trust.

sentences.zh: 檄既下，裁兵洶洶亡所歸。

translations.literal: Once the order was issued, the disbanded soldiers were in an uproar with nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: Once the order went out, the disbanded soldiers were in uproar with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 總督徐國相還朝已登舟，眾圍訴索餉，不得，遂大譁。

translations.literal: Governor-General Xu Guoxiang, returning to court, had already boarded his boat; the crowd surrounded him pleading for pay; when they did not obtain it, they raised a great clamor.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Xu Guoxiang had boarded his boat to return to court. The troops surrounded him demanding pay; denied, they raised a great clamor.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫柯永昇初上官，映榴攝布政使才三日。

translations.literal: At that time Governor Ke Yongsheng had just taken office; Yingliu had been acting Provincial Administration Commissioner for only three days.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ke Yongsheng had just taken office. Yingliu had been acting Provincial Administration Commissioner for only three days.

sentences.zh: 事急，映榴白永昇，請予兩月糧遣散，不許。

translations.literal: The matter was urgent; Yingliu told Yongsheng and asked that two months' grain be given to disperse them; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yingliu urgently asked Yongsheng to grant two months' grain to disperse the troops. Yongsheng refused.

sentences.zh: 眾入巡撫署，露刃呼譟。

translations.literal: The crowd entered the governor's yamen with bared blades, shouting and clamoring.
translations.idiomatic: The troops entered the governor's yamen with bared blades, shouting and clamoring.

sentences.zh: 映榴复白永昇，請好言慰遣之。

translations.literal: Yingliu again told Yongsheng and asked that soothing words be used to send them away.
translations.idiomatic: Yingliu again urged Yongsheng to soothe them and send them away.

sentences.zh: 永昇出，眾語不遜，永昇曰：「若輩欲反邪？

translations.literal: Yongsheng came out; the crowd's words were insolent; Yongsheng said: 'Do you want to rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Yongsheng came out. The troops were insolent. Yongsheng said: 'Do you mean to rebel?

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「反也奈何？

translations.literal: ' The crowd said: 'If we rebel, what of it?
translations.idiomatic: ' They answered: 'If we rebel, what then?

sentences.zh: 」刃傷永昇臂，奪其印，复刃傷足，僕，遂擁映榴至閱馬場。

translations.literal: ' They wounded Yongsheng's arm with a blade, seized his seal, again wounded his foot and servants, and thereupon dragged Yingliu to the horse-review ground.
translations.idiomatic: ' They slashed Yongsheng's arm, seized his seal, wounded his foot and servants, and dragged Yingliu to the horse-review ground.

sentences.zh: 永昇得間自經死。

translations.literal: Yongsheng found an opening and strangled himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yongsheng found a moment and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 逢龍自號「總統兵馬大元帥」，幟以白，迫布政使以下官受偽職，映榴紿以無殺掠，三日後徐議之。

translations.literal: Fenglong styled himself 'Grand Marshal President of Troops and Horses,' used white banners, and forced officials from the Provincial Administration Commissioner down to accept false offices; Yingliu deceived him by saying there would be no killing or plundering and that they would discuss it slowly after three days.
translations.idiomatic: Fenglong styled himself 'Grand Marshal President of Troops and Horses,' raised white banners, and forced officials to accept false offices. Yingliu stalled him with promises of no killing or plunder and discussion in three days.

sentences.zh: 乃令其妻陳奉母吳自水溝出，解印付其僕，乃手具遺疏。

translations.literal: He then had his wife Chen escort his mother Wu out through Shuigou, gave his seal to his servant, and personally wrote his final memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his wife Chen to escort his mother Wu out through Shuigou, gave his seal to a servant, and wrote his final memorial by hand.

sentences.zh: 是月丁酉，朝服升公座，罵賊，拔佩刀自刎死。

translations.literal: On dingyou of that month, in court dress he ascended the official seat, cursed the rebels, drew his girdle knife and cut his throat to death.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou of that month he ascended the official seat in court dress, cursed the rebels, and cut his throat with his girdle knife.

sentences.zh: 疏略曰：「臣一介豎儒，叨沐皇上高厚深恩，歷擢今職。

translations.literal: The memorial in summary said: 'Your servant is a mere rustic scholar who has received the Emperor's lofty, deep grace and has been promoted repeatedly to my present office.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial read in part: 'Your servant is a mere rustic scholar who has received the Emperor's profound grace and risen to my present office.

sentences.zh: 嘗以潔己奉公，自矢夙夜，但媿才具庸劣，未效寸長。

translations.literal: I have always sought to keep myself pure and serve the public, pledging myself day and night, but I am ashamed that my talent is mediocre and I have achieved no measure of good.
translations.idiomatic: I have sought purity in office and pledged myself day and night, yet my talent is mediocre and I have achieved little.

sentences.zh: 茲值裁兵夏逢龍倡亂，劫奪撫臣敕印，分兵圍臣衙門，露刃逼脅。

translations.literal: Now, at the disbanding of troops, Xia Fenglong has raised rebellion, seized the governor's commission and seal, and divided his forces to surround my yamen, baring blades to coerce me.
