translations.idiomatic: Now, as troops were disbanded, Xia Fenglong has rebelled, seized the governor's commission and seal, surrounded my yamen, and threatened me with bare blades.

sentences.zh: 臣幼讀詩書，粗知節義，雖斧鑕在前，豈肯喪恥偷生？

translations.literal: Your servant read the classics in youth and knows something of integrity; though the axe and halberd stand before me, how could I disgrace myself and live in stealth?
translations.idiomatic: I read the classics in youth and know something of integrity. Though execution awaits, how could I live in shame?

sentences.zh: 臣母年七十有六，在臣任所；

translations.literal: My mother is seventy-six and at my post;
translations.idiomatic: My mother is seventy-six and at my post;

sentences.zh: 臣長子旉，遠在原籍；

translations.literal: my eldest son Fu is far away in our native place;
translations.idiomatic: my eldest son Fu is far away in our native place;

sentences.zh: 其餘二子尚未成童，煢煢孤嫠，死將安歸？

translations.literal: my other two sons are not yet grown; lonely widows and orphans—where shall they go in death?
translations.idiomatic: my other two sons are still children. Where shall these lonely widows and orphans turn?

sentences.zh: 因遣妻女奉母潛逃。

translations.literal: I therefore sent my wife and daughters to escort my mother in secret flight.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore sent my wife and daughters to escort my mother away in secret.

sentences.zh: 臣如微服匿影，或可倖免以圖後效。

translations.literal: If your servant were to change clothes and hide, he might perhaps escape to seek later service.
translations.idiomatic: Had I changed clothes and hidden, I might have escaped to serve another day.

sentences.zh: 伏念臣守土之官也，城存與存，城亡與亡，義所當然。

translations.literal: But reflecting that I am an official charged with guarding the soil—when the city stands I stand, when it falls I fall—this is righteousness itself.
translations.idiomatic: But I am charged with guarding this soil. When the city stands I stand; when it falls I fall. That is righteousness.

sentences.zh: 今勉盡一死，以報國恩。

translations.literal: Now I strive to give my utmost in death to repay the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Now I give my death to repay the state's grace.

sentences.zh: 所恨事起倉猝，既不能先事綢繆，默消反側；

translations.literal: What I regret is that the matter arose in haste and I could not plan beforehand to quietly quell unrest;
translations.idiomatic: I regret that events arose in haste and I could not plan ahead to quell unrest;

sentences.zh: 復不能臨期捍禦，獨守孤城。

translations.literal: nor could I, when the moment came, defend and hold a lone city by myself.
translations.idiomatic: nor, when the moment came, defend this city alone.

sentences.zh: 上辜三十載之皇恩，下棄七旬餘之老母，君親兩負，死有餘慚。

translations.literal: Above I fail thirty years of imperial grace; below I abandon a mother of more than seventy; I have failed both sovereign and parent, and in death I have more than enough shame.
translations.idiomatic: I fail thirty years of imperial grace above and abandon a mother of more than seventy below. I have failed both sovereign and parent, and death itself brings shame enough.

sentences.zh: 」上覽疏，深愍傷之，召廷臣展讀，聞者皆感泣。

translations.literal: ' When the Emperor read the memorial, he was deeply moved with compassion; he summoned the court ministers to read it aloud, and all who heard wept.
translations.idiomatic: ' When the Emperor read the memorial he was deeply moved. He summoned ministers to read it aloud, and all who heard wept.

sentences.zh: 下部議卹，部議援陳丹赤例，贈通政使，特旨贈工部侍郎。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ministry for funeral honors; the ministry cited Chen Danchi's precedent and recommended posthumous Commissioner of the Court of State Ceremonial; a special edict made him Vice Minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry cited Chen Danchi's precedent and recommended Commissioner of the Court of State Ceremonial. A special edict made him Vice Minister of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 次年上南巡，旉迎謁，手書「忠節」二字賜之，遂以為諡。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Emperor made a southern tour, Fu came to pay respects; the Emperor personally wrote the two characters 'Loyal Integrity' and bestowed them, and this became his posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, during the southern tour, Fu came to pay respects. The Emperor wrote 'Loyal Integrity' and bestowed it as his posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 立祠武昌，書「丹心炳冊」扁以賜。

translations.literal: A shrine was built at Wuchang, and the inscription 'A Loyal Heart Illumines the Records' was written and bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was built at Wuchang, with the imperial inscription 'A Loyal Heart Illumines the Records.'

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，錄忠臣後，授其子旉鳳陽知府；

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, descendants of loyal ministers were recorded; his son Fu was appointed prefect of Fengyang;
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 8 (1730), descendants of loyal ministers were honored. His son Fu was appointed prefect of Fengyang;

sentences.zh: 芳蔚州知州，尋改員外郎；

translations.literal: Fang was made prefect of Weizhou, and shortly afterward was changed to secretary;
translations.idiomatic: Fang was made prefect of Weizhou, then secretary;

sentences.zh: 孫鳳毛內閣中書。

translations.literal: grandson Fengmao was made secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: grandson Fengmao was made secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與映榴同時死者，都司宣德仁，贈副將。

translations.literal: Those who died at the same time as Yingliu included Regional Vice Commander Xuan Deren, posthumously made deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died with Yingliu included Regional Vice Commander Xuan Deren, posthumously made deputy commander.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：功令褒死事，倉卒遇變與艱難效死者同，所以獎忠義也。

translations.literal: Commentary says: The statutes praise death in office; dying suddenly in crisis and dying after hard service are treated the same, in order to reward loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Statutes praise death in office. Sudden death in crisis and death after hard service are rewarded alike, to encourage loyalty.

sentences.zh: 莫洛與福，先事宜知有變，師行有進無退，雖死不撓。

translations.literal: Mo Luo and Fu, beforehand ought to have known there would be trouble; on campaign one advances and does not retreats—even in death they did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Luo and Fu should have foreseen trouble. On campaign one advances, never retreats—even in death they did not yield.

sentences.zh: 之鼎效忠於孤城，興元抗節於大憝。

translations.literal: Zhiding was loyal in a lone city; Xingyuan held to his integrity against a great villain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiding was loyal in a besieged city; Xingyuan held his integrity against a great rebel.

sentences.zh: 若啟泰、丹赤、映榴，皆能死其官者。

translations.literal: As for Qitai, Danchi, and Yingliu, all were able to die in their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Qitai, Danchi, and Yingliu all died at their posts.

sentences.zh: 啟泰以其家殉，與馬雄鎮比烈；

translations.literal: Qitai sacrificed his whole household, comparable in fervor to Ma Xiongzhen;
translations.idiomatic: Qitai sacrificed his whole household, a fervor comparable to Ma Xiongzhen;

sentences.zh: 映榴遺疏款款，則又范承謨蒙谷自序之亞也。

translations.literal: Yingliu's final memorial, so earnest and full, ranks next only to Fan Chengmo's preface at Menggu.
translations.idiomatic: Yingliu's earnest final memorial ranks next only to Fan Chengmo's preface at Menggu.
